passage.title: Life in a Growing City
passage.text: Cities are becoming larger as more people move from rural areas to urban areas. An urban area usually has many buildings, businesses, schools, and public services. In contrast, a rural area has more open land, farms, and smaller communities. As cities grow, good infrastructure becomes increasingly important. Roads, public transport, hospitals, schools, and other facilities help people live and work comfortably. Without enough infrastructure, a city may have problems providing basic services to its growing population. Housing is another important issue in large cities. Many people want to live near their workplaces, schools, and shopping areas. However, housing in central areas can be expensive. Some people therefore choose to live in a suburb, where homes may be more affordable and the environment can be quieter. Large cities often have many tall buildings. A skyscraper can provide offices or homes for a large number of people in a limited area. However, the growing population can also create congestion, especially during busy hours. To reduce congestion, some cities are creating safer areas for pedestrians. Wider sidewalks and pedestrian streets can encourage people to walk instead of using cars. A large city can offer many opportunities, but it also needs careful planning. Good infrastructure, suitable housing, and better transport can help create a more comfortable urban environment.

passage.title: The Challenges of a Megacity
passage.text: Modern cities continue to attract people because they provide employment, education, healthcare, and other opportunities. As populations increase, some cities develop into very large urban centres known as megacities. Managing these places requires careful planning and long-term investment. One of the main differences between urban and rural areas is population density. Urban areas usually contain more people and buildings in a smaller space, while rural areas tend to have more open land. As people move from the countryside to cities, the demand for housing increases. Providing enough housing can be difficult. In many cities, the cost of homes in central areas is high. Some residents move to the suburb, where residential areas may offer more space. However, living farther from the city centre can increase travel time. Good infrastructure is essential for a growing city. Roads, public transport, water systems, hospitals, schools, and other public facilities must be developed to meet the needs of residents. If infrastructure does not grow at the same speed as the population, services can become overcrowded. Another major problem is congestion. Large numbers of cars and other vehicles can make roads extremely busy, especially during peak hours. This can increase travel time and create air pollution. One possible solution is to make cities more friendly to pedestrians. Safe sidewalks, pedestrian streets, and crossings can encourage people to walk. Better public transport can also reduce the number of private vehicles on the roads. Tall buildings, including skyscrapers, are another common feature of modern cities. They allow businesses and residents to use limited land efficiently. However, very high buildings also require strong infrastructure and careful planning. A successful megacity must balance economic development with the quality of life of its residents. Urban planners need to consider housing, transport, infrastructure, public spaces, and environmental conditions together. Although city life can be challenging, well-planned urban development can make cities more convenient, efficient, and comfortable places to live.

passage.title: Living in a Growing City
passage.transcript: Today, I want to talk about life in a growing city. An urban area usually has many buildings, businesses, schools, and public services. A rural area, on the other hand, usually has more open land and fewer buildings. When more people move to cities, the need for good infrastructure increases. Cities need roads, public transport, hospitals, schools, and other facilities. Another important issue is housing. Homes in city centres can be expensive, so some people choose to live in a suburb. Suburbs can provide more space and a quieter environment. Large cities often have tall buildings called skyscrapers. These buildings can provide homes and offices without using too much land. However, large populations can also cause congestion. Roads may become very busy when many people travel to work or school. One way to improve city life is to create safer areas for pedestrians. Wider sidewalks and pedestrian streets can encourage people to walk. Some very large cities are called megacities. These cities need careful planning because they have large populations and many different needs. With good planning and suitable infrastructure, cities can become more comfortable places for residents to live and work.
